- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided several BBQ sauce recipes:
  - Kansas City-Style BBQ Sauce: 1 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
  - Spicy Peach BBQ Sauce: 1 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup peach preserves, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp hot sauce, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
  - Alabama-Style White BBQ Sauce: 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp chopped fresh dill, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, salt, and pepper.
  - Carolina-Style Vinegar-Based BBQ Sauce: 1 cup apple cider vinegar, 1/2 cup water, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp red pepper flakes (optional).
  - Jamaican Jerk BBQ Sauce: 1 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup pineapple juice, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp jerk seasoning, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp thyme, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
  - Bourbon BBQ Sauce: 1 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup bourbon whiskey, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
- [USER] The user has been wanting to try out a bourbon BBQ sauce and asked for tips on incorporating bourbon without it being too overpowering.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for incorporating bourbon into BBQ sauce:
  - Start with a small amount (2-3 tablespoons per cup of BBQ sauce).
  - Choose the right bourbon (wheated, high-rye, or higher proof).
  - Balance with sweetness (brown sugar, honey, or molasses).
  - Consider the type of BBQ sauce (thicker sauces work better).
  - Add bourbon towards the end of cooking.
  - Taste and adjust seasoning.
  - Infuse bourbon into other ingredients (e.g., whiskey-soaked wood chips).
  - Experiment with different ages of bourbon.
